title: Which Desert Father Are You?
description: Sixteen centuries ago, a handful of remarkable people walked into the Egyptian desert. Which one thinks like you?

questions.text: Your friends can't agree on weekend plans. You:

answers.text: Suggest the thing none of you have tried before
Propose one simple plan and get everyone to commit
Stay out of it and go along with whatever wins
Ask each person what they actually want most

questions.text: You join a new team where nothing is written down. First move:

answers.text: Start a shared doc so everyone knows who does what
Watch for two weeks before offering an opinion
Make sure the newest person doesn't feel lost
Take the smallest, dullest task and do it well

questions.text: Someone you know makes a big, public mistake. You:

answers.text: Stay out of the conversation about it entirely
Sit with them so they're not alone in it
Check in privately with one gentle question
Work out what led up to it, step by step

questions.text: Which compliment would mean the most?

answers.text: 'You never once made me feel small'
'Talking to you made everything feel simpler'
'You kept going after it stopped being fun'
'You did it first, when nobody else would'

questions.text: Your notes app is mostly full of:

answers.text: Things people told you that you don't want to forget
Reminders for tiny daily habits
Lists, categories, and patterns you've noticed
Schedules and checklists for other people

questions.text: A free Saturday, zero obligations. You:

answers.text: Do the chore you've put off, cheerfully
Finally read the thing you've meant to understand
Drive somewhere far, alone, with no plan
Stay home. No plans, no music, no talking.

questions.text: You're completely overwhelmed. What actually helps?

answers.text: Naming exactly what you're feeling and why
Getting away from everyone for a few days
Writing a list and doing item one
Helping someone else with theirs first

questions.text: Group project. Which role do you take without being asked?

answers.text: Starting the part everyone else is avoiding
Building the timeline everyone follows
Making sure nobody gets blamed for the slow week
Doing the tedious cleanup at the very end

questions.text: A party where you know almost nobody. You:

answers.text: Get a game going so people actually mix
Find the porch and stay there
End up in one long conversation with a stranger
Quietly map out who knows whom

questions.text: Your idea of a genuinely good morning:

answers.text: Nobody speaks to you for the first hour
Breakfast made for whoever happens to be around
The same routine, same order, every single day
Out the door before sunrise, no destination

questions.text: A friend keeps repeating the same mistake. You:

answers.text: Keep welcoming them exactly the same way
Wait until they ask, then say one true thing
Point out the pattern you've been noticing
Help them build a setup where it's harder to slip
Being asked for advice by someone not ready to hear it
Trusting something small matters when nothing's changed yet
Being needed by everyone right when you'd settled in
Small talk you can't politely escape

questions.text: Pick the book you'd actually finish:

answers.text: A short one, a page a night, for a whole year
A dense one you take notes on
A practical guide you start using immediately
The one a friend loved and lent to you

questions.text: Your default reaction to a strong emotion:

answers.text: Trace where it came from before acting on it
Face it head-on instead of distracting yourself
Step outside and mention it to no one
Talk it through with one trusted person

results.description: The one who went first. You're drawn to the hard, unmapped thing, you can outlast almost anyone, and people keep following you into places you only meant to explore alone.
You walked away from the noise and never missed it. Few words, deep attention, and a stillness other people find steadying — which is why, when you do speak, everyone listens.
You want to understand the machinery behind things — moods, motives, patterns. You can name what other people can only feel, and your clarity helps everyone else make sense of themselves.
Cheerful, stubborn faithfulness. You'll do the small unglamorous thing every single day long after everyone else has quit — and somehow you're still in a good mood about it.
You know what it costs to change, so you refuse to keep score on anyone else. Your welcome comes with no conditions, and people find it impossible to feel judged around you.
You turn scattered effort into something that actually works. Where others see chaos you see a workable plan, and the structures you quietly build end up holding everyone else up.
People bring you their tangles and leave lighter. You ask better questions than you give answers, and your advice is short, kind, and disarmingly practical.
